h: PCOS infertility: clomiphene mechanism?
p: Clomiphene is a SERM antagonist at the hypothalamus, removing negative feedback so GnRH, FSH and LH rise and induce ovulation. PCOS features: oligomenorrhea, hirsutism, high LH:FSH.

h: Severe asthma exacerbation: bedside sign?
p: Large intrathoracic pressure swings in severe obstruction produce pulsus paradoxus (inspiratory SBP drop above 10 mmHg), a marker of severity; silent chest is ominous.

h: Desmin-positive tumor?
p: Desmin is a muscle intermediate filament; rhabdomyosarcoma is also associated with TP53 (Li-Fraumeni). Melanoma is S-100 and HMB-45 positive.

h: Detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia after spinal cord injury: drug?
p: Alpha blockers relax the internal sphincter to allow emptying; bethanechol and neostigmine would worsen obstruction.

h: Thalidomide (phocomelia): current therapeutic use?
p: Thalidomide is teratogenic (limb defects) but now treats multiple myeloma and erythema nodosum leprosum. Isotretinoin treats acne; warfarin treats DVT.

h: Age-related high-frequency hearing loss: site of damage?
p: Presbycusis is sensorineural loss of high-frequency hair cells at the cochlear base; otosclerosis (stapes fixation) causes conductive loss.

h: CD8 T cell activation needs help from which cytokine?
p: CD8 T cells bind MHC I via CD8; full activation needs IL-2 (often from Th1 cells). IL-4 drives Th2/IgE; IL-8 recruits neutrophils.

h: Healthy toddler with a harsh holosystolic murmur: usual septal defect?
p: VSD is the most common congenital heart defect, usually membranous; small defects are asymptomatic and often close spontaneously, large ones cause shunting and heart failure.

h: Oligohydramnios, flat face, low-set ears, clubfeet, respiratory distress: cause?
p: No fetal urine means oligohydramnios, causing pulmonary hypoplasia, limb deformities and Potter facies.

h: AIDS with progressive multifocal neurologic deficits: virus family?
p: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy: JC virus reactivation destroys oligodendrocytes; MRI shows non-enhancing white matter lesions.

h: Older man with night back pain and weak urinary stream: likely cause?
p: Night pain, age over 50 and urinary symptoms point to prostate cancer with vertebral metastases; red-flag back pain needs imaging.

h: Newborn with hoarse cry, macroglossia, umbilical hernia, jaundice: cause?
p: Congenital hypothyroidism (cretinism) from thyroid dysgenesis presents with lethargy, large tongue, hypotonia and prolonged jaundice; newborn screening and levothyroxine prevent intellectual disability.

h: Hepatic angiosarcoma: occupational exposure?
p: Angiosarcoma of the liver is linked to vinyl chloride, arsenic and thorotrast; hepatitis B and cirrhosis cause hepatocellular carcinoma.

h: Carotid sinus massage for SVT: afferent nerve?
p: Baroreceptor afferents travel in CN IX (carotid sinus) and CN X (aortic arch); the efferent limb is the vagus, slowing AV node conduction.

h: Klinefelter syndrome: increased cancer risk?
p: 47,XXY men have a markedly higher risk of male breast cancer, plus gynecomastia, infertility and mediastinal germ cell tumors. Optic glioma is NF1; leukemia is Down syndrome.

h: Hypoxia after stopping nitrous oxide: cause?
p: Nitrous oxide rapidly leaves blood and dilutes alveolar oxygen; give 100% oxygen for 5-10 minutes at the end of anesthesia.

h: Sickle cell with fever, low reticulocytes, empty marrow: which crisis?
p: Parvovirus B19 infects erythroid progenitors, halting production (reticulocytes under 1 percent); sequestration shows high reticulocytes and splenomegaly.

h: Down syndrome with early dementia: mechanism?
p: The APP gene is on chromosome 21, so trisomy accelerates beta-amyloid deposition and early-onset Alzheimer disease in the 40s-50s.

h: Girl with developmental regression after age 1, hand-wringing: gene?
p: Rett syndrome (X-linked dominant, almost all girls): loss of speech and purposeful hand use, stereotyped hand movements, seizures; FMR1 causes fragile X.

h: Left pelvis sags when standing on the right leg: injured nerve?
p: Positive Trendelenburg: the superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius and minimus (hip abduction) on the standing side; the pelvis drops on the opposite side.

x: sickle crisis vs aplastic anemia ambiguity

h: Gowers sign in a clumsy 4-year-old boy: defect?
p: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (X-linked frameshift): calf pseudohypertrophy, proximal weakness, high CK, cardiomyopathy; Becker is milder with reduced dystrophin.

h: Solitary, emotionally cold, no desire for relationships, no odd beliefs: diagnosis?
p: Schizoid (cluster A) people prefer solitude and appear indifferent to praise; avoidant people desire relationships but fear rejection.

h: Brief morning stiffness, knee crepitus, DIP and PIP bony nodes: diagnosis?
p: Osteoarthritis: Heberden (DIP) and Bouchard (PIP) nodes, stiffness under 30 minutes, pain with activity; rheumatoid arthritis has prolonged stiffness and spares DIP.

h: Cup-to-disc ratio 0.9 with optic disc pallor: diagnosis?
p: Chronic open-angle glaucoma causes painless peripheral then central vision loss with optic cupping; treat to lower intraocular pressure (prostaglandin analogs, timolol).
